tone_statements.quote: The data from Swanton & Mendoza Ruíz (forthcoming:fn.10) are preliminary, i.e. the documentation and analysis are ongoing. The tone system of this variety is not further elaborated on, but the correspondences are very systematic. Tones are marked with numbers in this source (C3). This variety has three level tones (low, mid, high) and one contour tone (falling). The high tone does not appear on the first mora and the contour only appears in the second mora combining with a mid tone. This results in 7 contrastive tone melodies. The glottal stop does not affect tones.
tone_statements.locator: Supplementary Material 'Standardization of tone notations', p. 5, section 'Santa María Zacatepec Mixtec' and Table 7 'Contrastive melodies in Zacatepec Mixtec'
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (L, M, H) + 1 falling contour; 7 couplet melodies

tone_statements.citation: Towne, Douglas. 2011. Gramática popular del tacuate (mixteco) de Santa María Zacatepec, Oaxaca. (Serie gramáticas de lenguas indígenas de México 12.) México, D.F.: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. vii+140 pp. (electronic edition May 2012, downloaded via the Internet Archive from www-01.sil.org)
tone_statements.quote: Cada vocal del tacuate tiene un tono que forma una parte integral de la palabra. Es decir, para hablar correctamente hay que saber qué tono tiene cada vocal. Si no se pronuncia bien el tono, la palabra tiene otro significado, o sea, es otra palabra. Hay tres niveles de tono. En los ejemplos de abajo indicamos el tono alto con el acento agudo (á), el tono medio con una raya sobre la vocal (ā) y el tono bajo con una raya debajo de la vocal (a̱).
tone_statements.translation: Every vowel of Tacuate has a tone that forms an integral part of the word. That is, to speak correctly one must know which tone each vowel has. If the tone is not pronounced correctly, the word has another meaning, i.e. it is a different word. There are three tone levels. In the examples below we mark high tone with the acute accent (á), mid tone with a line over the vowel (ā) and low tone with a line under the vowel (a̱).
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (alto, medio, bajo); tense/aspect glides from tone combination

sources.note: Ch. 2 'El alfabeto tacuate' (pp. 5-10) covers vowels (plain, long, 'cortadas' = glottalized, nasalized), three level tones and their lexical/grammatical functions, consonants, loans; no statement of where word stress falls. Only accent-related remark is p. 97 (§12.2): enclitic adverbs -ni 'nada más' and -ga 'más' 'no tiene acento propio' and are therefore written attached to the preceding word. 'acento' elsewhere = orthographic diacritics for tone.

tone.says: §2.1.5 'Los tonos' (pp. 7-9): every vowel bears a tone; three tone levels (alto á, medio ā, bajo a̱) with 7 lexical minimal pairs (ma̱á 'mapache' vs māā 'madre', īín 'nueve' vs īīn 'uno', kuākú 'reirá' vs kuākū 'llorará'..); practical orthography leaves tone unmarked except acute on confusable pairs; grammatical tone: low tone on first vowel of verb = present, mid = past (combining with the root tone to create glides), high tone (written ä) = negative future, low tone derives adjectives from no…

sources.note: pp. 56-58: brief phonological profile (18 consonants, 5 vowels, vowel types, three level tones + rising/falling contours with minimal pairs); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Peña Flores, Esmeralda. 2023. Frases nominales en tu'un va'a (mixteco) de Santa María Zacatepec, Oaxaca. Tesis de maestría, Universidad de Sonora (Hermosillo). 155 pp.
sources.note: §2.3.1-2.3.2 (pp. 33-38): consonant and vowel inventory, open syllables only, modal vs non-modal (glottalized/rearticulated) vowels, three level tones plus contour tones, tonal aspect marking on first syllable of verb root. No mention of stress/acento (the word 'acento' occurs only for tone diacritics).

sources.note: Supplement p. 5: Zacatepec Mixtec has three level tones (low, mid, high) and one contour tone (falling); high tone does not occur on the first mora and the falling contour only on the second mora combined with mid, giving 7 contrastive couplet melodies (Table 7: 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.31 in Chao numbers); final glottal stop (preserved in this variety) does not affect tone; all Proto-Mixtec *H-initial sets merge to mid-mid and *L-initial sets to mid-mid.low reflexes. Main paper models rates of tone change and phylogenetic signal across the Mixtec varieties incl. Zacatepec.
